findings.source_quote: τούτοις δὲ μετάνοια οὐκ ἔστι, θάνατος δὲ ἔστι, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο καὶ μέλανές εἰσι· καὶ γὰρ τὸ γένος αὐτῶν ἄνομόν ἐστιν.
findings.english_quote: Repentance is not available to them. Death is. They are black because their kind is lawless.
findings.issue: The simplified text omits the explicit backward causal connection expressed by διὰ τοῦτο: their blackness is connected to the preceding exclusion of repentance and presence of death. It retains lawlessness as an explanation but makes that the only expressed explanation.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “Repentance is not available to them. Death is. That is also why they are black, for their kind is lawless.”

findings.source_quote: Διατί, φημί, κύριε, τούτοις μετάνοιά ἐστι, τοῖς δὲ προτέροις οὐκ ἔστι; παρά τι γὰρ αἱ αὐταὶ αἱ πράξεις αὐτῶν εἰσί. Διὰ τοῦτο, φησί, τούτοις μετάνοια κεῖται, ὅτι οὐκ ἐβλασφήμησαν τὸν Κύριον αὐτῶν·
findings.english_quote: “Sir,” I said, “why can these people repent, but the first group cannot? Their actions are almost the same.”[b] He said, “These people can repent because they did not blaspheme their Lord or betray God’s servants.
findings.issue: The question and answer replace the source’s availability of repentance with the people’s ability or inability to repent. In particular, “the first group cannot” introduces an assertion about their capacity to perform repentance, whereas the selected source denies that repentance is available to them. This also obscures the repeated availability wording preserved elsewhere in the simplified edition.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “Sir,” I said, “why is repentance available to these people but not to the first group? Their actions are almost the same.” He said, “Repentance is available to these people because they did not blaspheme their Lord or become betrayers of God’s servants.” Retain the existing note markers in their appropriate positions.

summary: The standard edition faithfully covers the selected working Greek, including its severe repentance distinctions, urgency, penalty, speaker changes, and disclosed editorial choices. The simplified edition independently requires revision for a lost causal connection and a shift from repentance’s availability to personal capacity. The supplied reports support retaining the disclosed working reading “bare”; no competing witness is silently substituted. Acceptance is limited to source fidelity and disclosure within the supplied materials, not authentication of unseen manuscripts or exhaustive verification of the apparatus. Proposed corrections require fresh review.
